videos.title: Why Laws, Treaties, and Regulations Won’t Save Us from AI | For Humanity Ep. 77
videos.description: 📢 Take Action on AI Risk → http://www.safe.ai/act 📰 Get 40% off Ground News’ unlimited access Vantage Plan at https://ground.news/airisk → for only $5/month, explore how stories are framed worldwide and across the political spectrum. 💚 Support our Mission → https://www.every.org/guardrailnow/f/prevent-human-extinc   What if the biggest mistake in AI safety is believing that laws, treaties, and regulations will save us?  In this episode of For Humanity, John sits down with Peter Sparber, a former architect of Big Tobacco’s successful war against regulation, to confront a deeply uncomfortable truth: the AI industry is using the exact same playbook—and it’s working. Drawing on decades of experience inside Washington’s most effective lobbying operations, Peter explains why regulation almost always fails against powerful industries, how AI companies are already neutralizing political pressure, and why real change will never come from lawmakers alone.   Instead, he argues that the only path to meaningful AI safety is making unsafe AI bad for business—by injecting risk, liability, and uncertainty directly into boardrooms and C-suites. Peter reveals why AI doesn’t need to outsmart humanity to defeat regulation, it only needs money, time, and political cover. By exposing how industries evade oversight, delay enforcement, and co-opt regulators, this conversation re-frames AI safety around power, incentives, and accountability.   ⏰ Timestamps  00:00 Introduction  02:00 Why AI safety’s focus on regulation may be doomed  06:30 The Big Tobacco playbook — and why it still works  11:40 Why public opinion rarely changes policy  17:50 How lobbying quietly kills AI regulation  24:00 Poison-pill laws and toothless agencies  30:00 Why treaties and global agreements fail  36:30 How industries exploit enforcement gaps  43:00 Why regulation often benefits corporations  48:30 The Underwriters Laboratory model for AI  55:40 Making unsafe AI bad for business  01:02:00 Data centers, local backlash, and real leverage 01:09:00 Why near-term harms mobilize people faster than extinction  01:16:30 What actually gives hope for AI safety  01:23:00 Final thoughts and closing   🔎 Together, they explore:  - Why laws, treaties, and regulations repeatedly fail against powerful industries  - How Big AI is following Big Tobacco’s exact regulatory playbook  - Why public outrage rarely translates into effective policy  - How companies neutralize enforcement without breaking the law  - Why third-party standards may matter more than legislation  - How local resistance, liability, and investor pressure can change behavior  - Why making unsafe AI bad for business is the only strategy with teeth   🎙️ About For Humanity  A podcast from the AI Risk Network, hosted by John Sherman, making AI extinction risk kitchen-table conversation on every street.   📺 Subscribe for weekly conversations on how we can confront the AI extinction threat.   #AISafety #AIRegulation #ForHumanityPodcast #AIRisk #AIAlignment #TechPolicy #AGI #ArtificialIntelligence #AIAccountability

Ideal for founders, content creators, consultants, podcasters, and anyone tired of bots joining their calls or manually copying transcripts into ChatGPT.  ⚡ 10 FREE WORKFLOW SHORTCUTS INCLUDED: I created 10 custom workflow shortcuts you can download and use immediately: 1. videos.title: What is Cheminformatics?
videos.description: Ever wondered how scientists discover new drugs faster than ever before? Or how computers can predict whether a molecule might be toxic without any lab experiments? The answer lies in cheminformatics!  In this video, we explore the fascinating world of cheminformatics, a field that combines chemistry with computer science to solve complex chemical problems. Whether you're a student, aspiring scientist, or simply curious about how technology is transforming science, this guide is perfect for you.  What You'll Learn:  In this beginner-friendly video, we cover everything you need to know about cheminformatics, including what it is, why it matters, and how it's changing the world of science.  We start by explaining molecular representations like SMILES, InChI, and molecular fingerprints, which allow computers to understand chemical structures. Then we explore massive chemical databases such as PubChem, ChEMBL, and DrugBank that store millions of compounds for research.  The video dives deep into real-world applications, especially in drug discovery, where techniques like virtual screening, QSAR modeling, and ADMET prediction are accelerating the development of new medicines. It also discusses how cheminformatics impacts materials science and environmental research.  Finally, it introduces popular tools like RDKit and explores how machine learning and artificial intelligence are pushing the boundaries of what's possible in chemistry. Resources Mentioned:  PubChem: https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ ChEMBL: https://www.ebi.ac.uk/chembl/ ZINC Database: https://zinc.docking.org/ DrugBank: https://go.drugbank.com/ RDKit: https://www.rdkit.org/ Open Babel: http://openbabel.org/ DeepChem: https://deepchem.io/  If you found this video helpful, please give it a thumbs up and subscribe to the channel for more educational content on science and technology. videos.description: 🎯 Understanding Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA) — Made Simple  LDA is more than just a classification technique — it’s about separating data intelligently while preserving meaningful patterns.
